sasha: Heads up — seeing a spike of routing errors this morning. Looks like some clients are sending both X-API-Version: v1 and ?version=v2 in query. Console shows requests flapping between v1/v2 routes. Anyone else seeing this?

mike: Yup. Saw it around 08:10. In some clusters we pick up header, in others query param. Result: quota attribution split and some 5xxs. Example curl in logs: 
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-API-Version: v1' 'https://api.redwood.ai/generate?version=v2'
```

elaine: Oof. This will confuse tenants. Suggest an ephemeral "coalescing" grace where we pick a single version per token for a short TTL (so clients with mixed signals don't get double-charged). Console should surface a banner: "mixed client signals — auto-coalescing" w/ opt-out.

raj: Implementation note: routing shim can maintain a tiny in-memory map token -> chosen_version with TTL (30s default). Emit metric compat.mixed_signals{chosen=v1|v2,source=header|query}. We'll also log a sampled x-request-id for traceability. Watch out for memory pressure if TTL too long.

toni: SRE concern — hiding the mismatch might mask real client bugs. Recommend staged rollout: 1% shadowing (no action), 10% canary (coalesce), then 100%. Add circuit-breaker: if mixed_signals > 2% traffic or error rate increases, auto-disable. Also need runbook entries for quick rollback.

mike: From billing side: we must decide attribution. If we coalesce, do we count v1 or v2 tokens? That affects billing and quota calculation. My suggestion: attribute to the token's pinned version if present, otherwise attribute to the coalesced choice and surface an adjustment. Need legal/ops review.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: routing-grace-ttl=30s to canary cluster at 2026-06-10T08:00Z (sha: abcd1234) :rocket:

sasha: Sounds good. Proposed policy parameters to formalize: precedence order = [token_pin, header, query], default TTL = 30s, circuit-breaker threshold = 2%, metrics to emit = compat.mixed_signals, compat.coalesced_count, compat.action (sampled events). I'll draft an RFC with those fields and sample payloads.

elaine: Also add Console telemetry card: per-tenant mixed_signal rate, ability to opt out of auto-coalesce per tenant, and a history graph for the coalesced decisions. That'll reduce support tickets.

raj: I'll spike a prototype in the routing shim today. Plan: intercept at routing boundary, run precedence logic, set chosen_version into ephemeral map, route accordingly, and add response headers: X-Compat-Coalesced and X-Compat-TTL-Left for observability. We'll also emit compat.action events at 1/100 sample rate.

toni: Please include a runbook fragment: steps to revert (disable feature flag / set ttl=0), alerts to create (mixed_signals > 2% or quota imbalance > 1%), and how to trace sample ids back to ingress logs.

mike: I'll coordinate with Billing & Ops to define attribution rules and any retro adjustments. tagging: billing@redwood.

sasha: Quick question: do we want to set a response warning header so clients see they triggered coalescing? e.g., `X-Compat-Coalesced: v1` and `X-Compat-Reason: mixed_signals`

raj: +1 on warning header. We'll include `X-Compat-TTL-Left` too so retries can adjust.

sasha: Great — I'll put together the RFC and include mock console copy, metric names, and the rollout plan. Expecting draft by EOD. :thumbsup:
